title: Naphtha Redemption for LR1s?
summary: After languishing below operating costs for almost six months, LR1 earnings on the benchmark Baltic TC5 route, carrying 55,000 MT of naphtha AG-Japan, have more than doubled during the past two weeks, to above $13,000/day. The LR1 sector has suffered recently from brisk fleet growth, rising by 7.9% during 2011; slowing Asian industrial production growth, limiting petrochemical naphtha demand; competition with MRs for new Indian refinery naphtha production and elusive arbitrages. After collapsing to $1,000/day in October 2011, earnings on the TC5 route recovered slightly, but averaged only $5,200/day for 1q12.

children.title: LR1 & LR2 Spot TCE Earnings
children.summary: 55 AG-Japan TC5 FFA 2q12 The fortunes for LR1 reversed dramatically in early-April with a surge in naphtha fixtures from Asian ethylene producers, as 2.4 mtpa of naphtha cracker capacity in Japan and Korea came back on line during April, following Spring maintenance. This pick up in Asian activity out of the AG soaked up available supply, and as the Med-Japan naphtha arbitrage opened up modestly, traders secured additional tonnage for this long-haul route, further reducing AG availability.

children.title: Chart: vs Dubai Crude
children.summary: Although the continued growth of Chinese petrochemical demand would support continued naphtha demand, tempered by the rise in domestic refinery capacity, the near-term naphtha outlook is still clouded by the forward prospects for Asian industrial production. Singapore naphtha cracks versus Dubai crude are still languishing near minus $5/bbl, despite the surge in recent cargo buying.

children.title: Official PMI
children.summary: HSBC PMI The LR1 sector would benefit from a resumption in Asian industrial production growth, given its slowing tonnage supply, but current indicators suggest that an LR1 redemption may have to wait until later in the cycle. The spike in LR1 rates has been a welcome relief to owners, but looks unsustainable for the moment.
